assoc delete-assocs.help:
Deletes the associations between the sources and entities specified. 
[Command Reference](deleteAssociations)

params.name: namespace_name
params.help: The Log Analytics namespace used for the request. The namespace can be obtained by running 'oci os ns get' [required]

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The compartment ID

params.name: items
params.help:
The information required to delete an association.

This option is a JSON list with items of type DeleteLogAnalyticsAssociation.  For documentation on DeleteLogAnalyticsAssociation please see our API reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/api/#/en/loganalytics/20200601/datatypes/DeleteLogAnalyticsAssociation.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation asynchronously creates, modifies or deletes a resource and uses a work request to track the progress of the operation. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the work request to reach the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.

params.name: from_json
params.help:
Provide input to this command as a JSON document from a file using the file://path-to/file syntax.

The --generate-full-command-json-input option can be used to generate a sample json file to be used with this command option. The key names are pre-populated and match the command option names (converted to camelCase format, e.g. compartment-id --> compartmentId), while the values of the keys need to be populated by the user before using the sample file as an input to this command. For any command option that accepts multiple values, the value of the key can be a JSON array.

Options can still be provided on the command line. If an option exists in both the JSON document and the command line then the command line specified value will be used.

params.help:
The date and time the resource was last discovered, in the format defined by RFC3339.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

params.help: A list of tag filters to apply.  Only entities with a freeform tag matching the value will be returned. The key for each tag is "{tagName}.{value}".  All inputs are case-insensitive. Values for different keys (i.e. different namespaces, different tag names, or both) are interpreted as "AND".

All inputs are case-insensitive. Currently, only existence ("true" at the end) is supported. Absence ("false" at the end) is not supported. The date and time the resource was last discovered, in the format defined by RFC3339.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation creates, modifies or deletes a resource that has a defined lifecycle state. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the resource reaches a given lifecycle state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACTIVE --wait-for-state DELETED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. object-collection-rule create.help:
Creates a rule to collect logs from an object storage bucket. 
[Command Reference](createLogAnalyticsObjectCollectionRule)

params.name: namespace_name
params.help: The Log Analytics namespace used for the request. The namespace can be obtained by running 'oci os ns get' [required]

params.name: name
params.help: A unique name given to the rule. The name must be unique within the tenancy, and cannot be modified. [required]

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment to which this rule belongs. [required]

params.name: os_namespace
params.help: Object Storage namespace. [required]

params.name: os_bucket_name
params.help: Name of the Object Storage bucket. [required]

params.name: log_group_id
params.help: Log Analytics Log group OCID to associate the processed logs with. [required]

params.name: description
params.help: A string that describes the details of the rule. It does not have to be unique, and can be changed. Avoid entering confidential information.

params.name: collection_type
params.help: The type of collection.

params.name: poll_since
params.help: The oldest time of the file in the bucket to consider for collection. Accepted values are: BEGINNING or CURRENT_TIME or RFC3339 formatted datetime string. Use this for HISTORIC or HISTORIC_LIVE collection types. When collectionType is LIVE, specifying pollSince value other than CURRENT_TIME will result in error.

params.name: poll_till
params.help: The newest time of the file in the bucket to consider for collection. Accepted values are: CURRENT_TIME or RFC3339 formatted datetime string. Use this for HISTORIC collection type. When collectionType is LIVE or HISTORIC_LIVE, specifying pollTill will result in error.

params.name: log_source_name
params.help: Name of the Log Analytics Source to use for the processing.

params.name: entity_id
params.help: Log Analytics entity OCID. Associates the processed logs with the given entity (optional).

params.name: char_encoding
params.help: An optional character encoding to aid in detecting the character encoding of the contents of the objects while processing. It is recommended to set this value as ISO_8859_1 when configuring content of the objects having more numeric characters, and very few alphabets. For e.g. this applies when configuring VCN Flow Logs.

params.name: is_enabled
params.help: Whether or not this rule is currently enabled.

params.name: timezone
params.help: Timezone to be used when processing log entries whose timestamps do not include an explicit timezone. When this property is not specified, the timezone of the entity specified is used. If the entity is also not specified or do not have a valid timezone then UTC is used.

params.name: log_set
params.help: The logSet to be associated with the processed logs. The logSet feature can be used by customers with high volume of data and this feature has to be enabled for a given tenancy prior to its usage. When logSetExtRegex value is provided, it will take precedence over this logSet value and logSet will be computed dynamically using logSetKey and logSetExtRegex.

params.name: log_set_key
params.help: An optional parameter to indicate from where the logSet to be extracted using logSetExtRegex. Default value is OBJECT_PATH (e.g. /n/<namespace>/b/<bucketname>/o/<objectname>).

params.name: log_set_ext_regex
params.help: The regex to be applied against given logSetKey. Regex has to be in string escaped format.

params.name: overrides
params.help:
The override is used to modify some important configuration properties for objects matching a specific pattern inside the bucket. Supported propeties for override are: logSourceName, charEncoding, entityId. Supported matchType for override are "contains".
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: object_name_filters
params.help:
When the filters are provided, only the objects matching the filters are picked up for processing. The matchType supported is exact match and accommodates wildcard "*". For more information on filters, see [Event Filters].
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: log_type
params.help: Type of files/objects in this object collection rule.

params.name: is_force_historic_collection
params.help: Flag to allow historic collection if poll period overlaps with existing ACTIVE collection rule

params.name: stream_id
params.help: A Stream OCID is required for Object Collection rules of type LIVE or HISTORIC_LIVE, which will be used by Log Analytics while creating Event Rule and consume the event notifications created by the Object Storage.

params.name: stream_cursor_type
params.help: Cursor type used to fetch messages from stream. When the streamCursorType is set to DEFAULT, the existing cursor position will be used if already set by any previous objection collection rule(s) using the same stream. Otherwise, the behaviour is to consume from the oldest available message in the stream. When the streamCursorType is set to TRIM_HORIZON, the behaviour is to start consuming from the oldest available message in the stream. When the streamCursorType is set to LATEST, the behavior is to start consuming messages that were published after the creation of this rule. When the streamCursorType is set to AT_TIME, the behavior is to start consuming from a given time. For more information on cursor types, see [Stream Consumer Groups].

params.name: stream_cursor_time
params.help:
The time from which to consume the objects, if streamCursorType is AT_TIME.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

params.name: time_updated
params.help:
The last updated date.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

[Command Reference](disableAutoAssociation)

params.name: namespace_name
params.help: The Log Analytics namespace used for the request. The namespace can be obtained by running 'oci os ns get' [required]

params.name: source_name
params.help: The source name. [required]

params.name: items
params.help:
A list of information required to disable auto association on a source.

This option is a JSON list with items of type DisableAutoAssociationDetail.  For documentation on DisableAutoAssociationDetail please see our API reference: https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/api/#/en/loganalytics/20200601/datatypes/DisableAutoAssociationDetail.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation asynchronously creates, modifies or deletes a resource and uses a work request to track the progress of the operation. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the work request to reach the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.

params.name: from_json
params.help:
Provide input to this command as a JSON document from a file using the file://path-to/file syntax.

The --generate-full-command-json-input option can be used to generate a sample json file to be used with this command option. The key names are pre-populated and match the command option names (converted to camelCase format, e.g. compartment-id --> compartmentId), while the values of the keys need to be populated by the user before using the sample file as an input to this command. For any command option that accepts multiple values, the value of the key can be a JSON array.

params.name: time_updated
params.help:
The last updated date.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

params.name: if_match
params.help: For optimistic concurrency control. In the PUT or DELETE call for a resource, set the `if-match` parameter to the value of the etag from a previous GET or POST response for that resource. The resource will be updated or deleted only if the etag you provide matches the resource's current etag value.

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation asynchronously creates, modifies or deletes a resource and uses a work request to track the progress of the operation. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the work request to reach the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.

storage estimate-purge-data-size.help:
This API estimates the size of data to be purged based based on time interval, purge query etc. 
[Command Reference](estimatePurgeDataSize)

params.name: namespace_name
params.help: The Log Analytics namespace used for the request. The namespace can be obtained by running 'oci os ns get' [required]

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: This is the compartment OCID under which the data will be purged [required]

params.name: time_data_ended
params.help:
This is the time before which data will be purged
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400
    [required]

params.help: The name of the upload. This can be considered as a container name where different kind of logs will be collected and searched together. This upload name/id can further be used for retrieving the details of the upload, including its status or deleting the upload.

params.name: entity_id
params.help: The entity OCID.

params.name: timezone
params.help: Timezone to be used when processing log entries whose timestamps do not include an explicit timezone. When this property is not specified, the timezone of the entity specified is used. If the entity is also not specified or do not have a valid timezone then UTC is used

params.name: char_encoding
params.help: Character encoding to be used to detect the encoding type of file(s) being uploaded. When this property is not specified, system detected character encoding will be used.

params.name: date_format
params.help: This property is used to specify the format of the date. This is to be used for ambiguous dates like 12/11/10. This property can take any of the following values -  MONTH_DAY_YEAR, DAY_MONTH_YEAR, YEAR_MONTH_DAY, MONTH_DAY, DAY_MONTH.

params.name: date_year
params.help: Used to indicate the year where the log entries timestamp do not mention year (Ex: Nov  8 20:45:56).

params.name: invalidate_cache
params.help: This property can be used to reset configuration cache in case of an issue with the upload.

params.name: content_md5
params.help:
The base-64 encoded MD5 hash of the body. If the Content-MD5 header is present, Log Analytics performs an integrity check on the body of the HTTP request by computing the MD5 hash for the body and comparing it to the MD5 hash supplied in the header. If the two hashes do not match, the log data is rejected and an HTTP-400 Unmatched Content MD5 error is returned with the message:

"The computed MD5 of the request body (ACTUAL_MD5) does not match the Content-MD5 header (HEADER_MD5)"

params.name: content_type
params.help: The content type of the log data.

params.name: log_set
params.help: The log set that gets associated with the uploaded logs.

params.help: A value of `100-continue` requests preliminary verification of the request method, path, and headers before the request body is sent. If no error results from such verification, the server will send a 100 (Continue) interim response to indicate readiness for the request body. The only allowed value for this parameter is "100-Continue" (case-insensitive).

warning list.help:

[Command Reference](listWarnings)

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The ID of the compartment in which to list resources. [required]

params.name: warning_state
params.help: The warning state used for filtering.  A value of SUPPRESSED will return only suppressed warnings, a value of UNSUPPRESSED will return only unsuppressed warnings, and a value of ALL will return all warnings regardless of their suppression state.  Default is UNSUPPRESSED.

params.name: source_name
params.help: The source name.

params.name: source_pattern
params.help: The source pattern used for filtering.  Only warnings associated with a source with the specified pattern will be returned.

params.name: warning_message
params.help: warning message query parameter

params.name: entity_name
params.help: The entity name used for filtering.

params.name: entity_type
params.help: The entity type used for filtering.  Only associations on an entity with the specified type will be returned.

params.name: warning_type
params.help: The warning type query parameter.

params.name: is_no_source
params.help: A flag indicating whether to filter warnings based on source display name or on warning level. A value of true will filter based on warning level (rule, source, or pattern), while a value of false will filter based on source display name.

params.name: start_time
params.help: The warning start date query parameter.

params.name: end_time
params.help: The warning end date query parameter.

params.name: limit
params.help: The maximum number of items to return.

params.name: page
params.help: The page token representing the page at which to start retrieving results. This is usually retrieved from a previous list call.

params.name: sort_order
params.help: The sort order to use, either ascending (`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`).

params.name: sort_by
params.help: The attribute used to sort the returned warnings

params.name: all_pages
params.help: Fetches all pages of results. If you provide this option, then you cannot provide the --limit option.

params.name: page_size
params.help: When fetching results, the number of results to fetch per call. Only valid when used with --all or --limit, and ignored otherwise.
